# Beta Negative Binomial Distribution

## Overview

The beta negative binomial distribution describes the probability of getting **k failures before getting r successes**, where the probability of each success is distributed with a beta distribution.

## Description

This is a compound distribution that adds another layer of complexity to the negative binomial distribution. Instead of assuming a fixed probability of success, the probability itself is modeled as a random variable drawn from a Beta distribution.

This creates a hierarchical model that accounts for extra-variability (over-dispersion) in the data.

## Probability Density Function

$$X \sim BNB(r, \alpha, \beta) = \int_0^1 f_{X | p }(k|r,q) \cdot f_p(q | \alpha, \beta) dq = \frac{B(r+k, \alpha + \beta)}{B(r, \alpha)} \frac{\Gamma(k + \beta)}{k!\Gamma(\beta)}$$

Where:
- $r$ = number of target successes
- $k$ = number of failures before achieving r successes
- $\alpha$, $\beta$ = parameters of the Beta distribution
- $B(\cdot)$ = Beta function
- $\Gamma(\cdot)$ = Gamma function

## Interpretation

This formula looks complex, but it can be explained more simply:

- $f_{X|p}(k|r,q)$ describes the conditional probability of drawing k failures before r successes, given probability q
- This is then integrated over all possible values of q, weighted by the Beta distribution
- The result accounts for uncertainty in the success probability

## Real-world Examples

- Number of patients screened before finding 10 eligible participants in a clinical trial (with variable eligibility rates)
- Number of attempts before achieving 5 successful reactions in chemistry experiments
- Number of customers before finding 20 buyers (with variable purchase rates)
